sources.entry: Hatsu - Bridge that interacts with Fediverse on behalf of your static site. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker/Rust

summary.one_liner: Hatsu is a self-hosted ActivityPub bridge that lets a static website take part in the Fediverse on its behalf.
summary.what_it_does: Hatsu runs alongside a static site and handles Fediverse interactions for it. When a Fediverse user searches for a user of the site (e.g. @catch-all@example.com), it redirects to the matching user on the Hatsu instance. When someone searches for a site URL, it redirects to the corresponding post on the Hatsu instance. It accepts follow requests and pushes new posts to followers as they become available, and it is described as able to receive replies from Fediverse users and backfeed them to the static site (the README marks backfeed as work in progress). The README says it uses Feed rather than Webmention to detect updates and does not require microformats2 on the site. It is written in Rust, ships with Docker support, and supports aarch64.
use_cases: Make a static blog visible to Fediverse users
Let Mastodon-style users follow a static site
Push new static site posts to Fediverse followers
Redirect Fediverse searches for site URLs to posts
Receive replies from Fediverse users on a static site
how_to_run: Read the documentation to get started (the README links no specific commands)
notable: Fully automated once configured, with no ongoing manual steps described
Works with any static site generator and most static hosts, using feed polling instead of Webmention
Does not require the site to support microformats2
Adds HTTP signed fetches for compatibility with Mastodon secure mode and GoToSocial
Built on the same federation library as Lemmy
caveats: Backfeed of replies to the static site is marked as work in progress
Setup details are not in the README; it defers to external documentation
Compatibility issues with other Fediverse software may be Hatsu-specific or upstream, per the README's advice to file issues in Hatsu first
